courseCorrections.GOSHIST112: Studies gendered lives, queer and heteronormative narratives, intersectionality and resistance in North American history. Primary sources, an older queer person interview, the Walking with Pride artwork and original research connect historical interpretation to identity and public culture.
courseCorrections.GOSHIST311: Studies Native American histories, institutional violence, intergenerational trauma, resistance, food sovereignty and cultural expression. Indigenous perspectives, arts-based collaboration and public-history work contribute specific cultural and historical inquiry.
courseCorrections.GOSPHIL212: Develops moral argument through utilitarian, Kantian, virtue, contractarian and feminist ethics, close reading and independent essays. These are complementary tools for evaluating responsibility and contested public choices; particular climate, privacy or cultural-policy cases are not guaranteed.
courseCorrections.DISARIN111: Examines AI ethics, fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political risks alongside psychological perspectives. Research synthesis, an analytical psychology project and a podcast support inquiry into digital society; a cultural-industry case is not prescribed.
courseCorrections.MCCMEDI211: Examines American social history through television, film and digital forms, including conformity, Indigenous self-representation and disability. Analysis and speculative television/futures projects connect storytelling, representation and power to cultural identity; this is not a generic platform-economics course.
courseCorrections.BENENTR311: Plans and carries out customer research, analyses findings and communicates business implications. Its actual research methods support inquiry into audiences and cultural organisations, without guaranteeing an arts-sector research topic.
courseCorrections.BENLEAD311: Studies motivation, groups, leadership, organisational culture, power and change. Organisational case research plans and a brief systematic literature review provide complementary management inquiry; cultural organisations are not guaranteed cases.

finding: Same three concepts/course sets retained after current-evidence comparability and distinctness challenge; two stale offering conflicts repaired. Complete course/project contributions considered without promoting independent course papers to a full empirical BA thesis.
